A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CURE research by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–E support comparison despite the changed title and extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original certified-robustness experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet, including geometric and patch evaluations, ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original vision experiments and adds results on CIFAR-100, SST-2 with BERT, geometric-training comparators and perturbation-strength analyses.

M1.justification: The core losses, bound alignment, gradient projection, fine-tuning and Algorithms 1–6 are retained. However, Appendix B changes the stated l2 search region from a truncated l2 ball to an l-infinity ball with l2-directed gradients. The unchanged pseudocode and retained introductory description leave an actual procedural change versus a documentation correction unresolved.

E1.justification: v3 adds CIFAR-100 image classification and SST-2 text classification with BERT under PWWS and TextFooler attacks (Tables 6, 2 and 12). This extends coverage to additional object classes and a language domain while retaining the original vision datasets and perturbation families.

E2.justification: v3 adds geometrically trained CGT models to the CIFAR-10 multi-norm comparison (Table 8) and FLAT to the SST-2 comparison (Table 12), introducing distinct comparator families. The earlier PGD-training and Hu et al. (2023) comparisons remain in Tables 11 and 14.

E3.justification: The BA/GP ablation changes from MNIST to CIFAR-10, and the beta sweep changes from the smaller CIFAR-10 perturbation setting to (8/255, 0.5, 1.0). v3 also expands hyperparameter and evaluation-epsilon sweeps, introduces an attack-coverage protocol, and evaluates BERT using empirical attacks as a certification proxy. The original CNN7 training budgets and certification sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of overlap with CGT bounds and successful attacks outside the other norm ball (Tables 9–10), plus robustness across perturbation strengths (Figures 7–9). It expands lambda2 and beta sensitivity analyses and replaces the MNIST BA/GP ablation with a CIFAR-10 ablation. Earlier bound visualizations and the alpha ablation are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The newly reported 19,968 PGD attacks describe evaluation sampling, not repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The TinyImageNet CURE-Scratch row changes from 28.1% clean and 18.2% union accuracy to 29.7% and 22.4% (v2 Table 2; v3 Table 1). Added results include 30.4% union accuracy on CIFAR-100 and 28.4%/17.6% empirical accuracy under PWWS/TextFooler on SST-2. New overlap, comparator and sensitivity results accompany the replaced ablation results; most original benchmark entries are retained.

T1.justification: Where v2 only states that its binary analysis can extend to multiclass classification, v3 supplies multiclass risk and margin definitions, a theorem and a proof in Appendix A.1.1. It also corrects the extreme-case alignment error from 1 − Rq to 1 − Rr and explicitly requires the disjoint attackable sets to cover the instance space (v2 Table 1; v3 Figure 3).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the principal CURE contributions, first multi-norm certified-training claim and headline vision improvements. Changing 'universal' to 'generalized' preserves the operational goal of transfer to geometric and patch perturbations; v2 already presented universality as an aspiration.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting non-lp generalization to bound overlap, discusses asymmetric norm conflicts and practical barriers to l1 training, and explicitly disclaims achieved universal robustness. It also qualifies the BERT results as empirical proxies rather than certificates and expands the interpretation of how bound alignment mitigates robustness conflicts.

D1.justification: The main hyperparameter table, hardware and certification sample counts are retained. v3 revises the l2 example-generation description and adds latent-space BERT and bound-overlap normalization details, but omits v2's code-availability statement and GitHub link. This establishes a disclosure change, not that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands discussion of certified training, empirical multi-norm defenses, practical applications and text attacks while removing some earlier verification references. New Section 5.3 explicitly explains dependence on prior adversarial-training ideas and distinguishes optimization of certified bounds from empirical adversarial objectives, sharpening the contribution's positioning.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the introduction, background, related work and method explanations. It places Background before Related Work, consolidates method subsections, adds a dedicated discussion and replaces the impact statement with acknowledgements. The title and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout, and Figure 1b is redrawn. The main results table is split between main text and appendix; MNIST and CIFAR-10 geometric displays exchange locations; patch and ablation tables are paired. New tables and epsilon-sweep plots substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: New dataset, comparator and perturbation-strength evaluations broaden empirical support, and the limitations are clearer. However, the added multiclass proof in Appendix A.1.1 equates unequal margins with a negative margin product, which fails for unequal positive margins. Together with the unresolved l2-search description and removed code-access disclosure, these mixed effects prevent a confident net quality judgment.
